title: Delhi HC: Customs Cannot Let Adjudication Delay Punish a Passenger With Mounting Demurrage
case_name: Niyamat Khan v. Commissioner of Customs, IGI Airport & Anr.
card_summary: Customs detained the petitioner's goods at IGI Airport in January 2025 but issued a personal hearing notice only in August 2025, while demurrage charges kept accumulating. A Division Bench of Justices Avneesh Jhingan and Shail Jain held that such delay in adjudication cannot work as a mode of punishment for the passenger, and directed Customs to file a detailed affidavit within three weeks.
card_tip: A passenger whose goods are detained at the airport should ask in writing for the show cause notice and a hearing date, rather than letting warehousing and demurrage charges run up while the file sits unattended.
verification_notes: The detention date (January 2025), the gap to the personal hearing notice (August 2025), the bench composition (Jhingan and Jain JJ), the 'mode of punishment' finding, the three-week affidavit direction and the suggestion on airport-wide data are consistent across the Devdiscourse and LiveLawBiz reports seen in this run, with A2Z Taxcorp corroborating the same facts.
